audit_findings.title: The valuation-date merger status may make both numerator and denominator stale
audit_findings.mechanism: A post-June closing would change the earnings perimeter, fully diluted shares, cash and investments, assumed obligations, and equity bridge; the filed exchange ratio is 0.3575 Axcelis share per Veeco share.
audit_findings.evidence: Axcelis and Veeco continue to expect that the Merger will be completed in the second half of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The August 6 filing demonstrates that the merger remained pending then, but does not establish its status on the September 6 valuation date. If it closed during that interval, the standalone valuation would be stale. Added Veeco economics could increase value, while new shares, obligations, and integration costs could reduce value per existing Axcelis share. The supplied record lacks Veeco's closing-date share count and combined financial position, so the effect is unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-August 6 current reports and closing announcements. If closing occurred by September 6, rerun with the effective-date issued shares, combined balance sheet, assumed obligations, and seasoned combined owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.357 million of 2025 principal, equal to 1.6% of the $83.1 million anchor; if wholly omitted, approximately $0.43-$0.67 per share across the filed scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Finance-lease principal is a financing cash outflow excluded from operating cash flow; if finance-lease depreciation was added back without a separate principal deduction, OE is overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: The associated lease payments include both an interest component and payment of principal, with the underlying liability being extinguished at the end of the original lease term.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate a $1.357 million 2025 principal payment and $1.193 million of finance-lease depreciation, but the supplied record does not prove whether the calculator separately deducted principal. Even assuming the entire principal payment was omitted, the computed valuation effect is only about $0.43-$0.67 per share, versus the $61.10 gap between the $53.98 bull value and the $115.08 market price. It therefore would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $1.193 million depreciation add-back and $1.357 million principal payment through the 2025 OE workpaper; deduct principal only if depreciation was added back and principal was not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Long-term investments may be stranded outside both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Portfolio interest income is purged from OE, but the bridge adds only $154.996 million of cash and $247.220 million of short-term investments; the separately filed long-term investments are omitted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We held $228.8 million of short-term investments and $182.4 million of long-term investments at December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission, not merely a possibility. The $402.216 million bridge equals June 30 cash plus short-term investments exactly, while the same balance sheet separately reports $174.829 million of long-term U.S. government and agency investments. Adding them would increase every scenario by $5.53 per share, a material 11.6% of the $47.68 base value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the securities were unrestricted and non-operating on September 6, then add the valuation-date fair value of qualifying long-term investments to the bridge and rerun all per-share values.

audit_findings.title: A material merger one-off contaminates the latest-actual anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.3 million pretax, equal to 19.6% of the $83.1 million anchor; full pretax removal would add approximately $5.19-$8.09 per share before tax and cash-timing adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: The latest-actual OE anchor is propagated through the forecast and terminal value, so any nonrecurring merger cash cost embedded in 2025 OE depresses all projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase was primarily due to an increase in merger-related professional and filing fees of $16.3, partially offset by a decrease in bad debt expense $3.0.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $16.3 million of incremental merger-related professional and filing expense, large relative to the anchor. It does not establish how much was paid in 2025 and therefore captured in cash-based OE, or the applicable tax effect. The possible valuation effect is nevertheless material. Future integration and restructuring costs are separate post-closing items and should not be netted against the demonstrated standalone transaction expense without evidence.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $16.3 million expense to 2025 cash payments, accrual changes, and tax treatment. Rerun standalone value after removing only the verified nonrecurring after-tax cash amount; perform a separate combined-company rerun after closing.

audit_findings.title: The bridge does not reserve for a potentially large merger termination claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $108.7 million conditional termination fee, or $3.44 per diluted share; alternatively, a $15.0 million reimbursement equals $0.47 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If an Axcelis payment obligation had been triggered by the valuation date, it would reduce cash or create a liability ahead of common equity in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If the Merger Agreement is terminated by a party following a recommendation change of the board of directors of the other party, the non-terminating party will be required to pay the other party the following termination fee: (i) if the non-terminating party is Axcelis, a termination fee of $ 108.7 million; and (ii) if the non-terminating party is Veeco, a termination fee of $ 77.5 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The fee amounts are filed, but no supplied evidence shows that a recommendation change, competing proposal, qualifying breach, or termination had occurred by September 6. Accordingly, no automatic deduction is justified. A crystallized $108.7 million claim would equal 7.2% of the $1.507 billion base equity value and is potentially material, while its existence at the valuation date remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Review post-quarter filings, board-recommendation disclosures, competing-proposal notices, breach notices, and merger-status announcements through September 6. Deduct the applicable fee or reimbursement and rerun only if a payment obligation had become probable or enforceable by that date.
